technical_and_design_decisions: Use existing Spring Boot and Spring Cloud conventions rather than introducing a new application framework or custom runtime.
Implement REST support for stream commands through Spring MVC/WebFlux controllers consistent with the existing StreamController design, with JSON request and response payloads.
Use shell-based curl or equivalent command-line scripts as repeatable validation and smoke tests for REST endpoints.
Adapt the Redis counter as a Spring Cloud Stream module, preserving the expected counter semantics and using the existing Redis client and configuration conventions where available.

Implement dependency resolution and Boot loader integration using Maven or Gradle artifact metadata and Spring Boot loader-compatible classpath handling, avoiding manual per-driver packaging where possible.
Bootify ModuleLauncher by converting it to a Spring Boot executable application with externalized configuration and an extension point for future classpath augmentation.

Treat the PHD/HDFS work as a technical investigation and prototype recommendation rather than a full production implementation, because the specification does not define the PHD API or supported HDFS versions.
Use repository-native continuous integration, assumed to be GitHub Actions, with build, test, packaging, and relevant static checks triggered on commits and pull requests.
Add automated unit, integration, and smoke coverage for the implemented behavior, using test doubles or embedded services where practical.
assumptions: The existing spring-cloud-data, spring-cloud-stream-modules, and related source repositories are available and buildable with Java 17 or a compatible required toolchain.
The developer is responsible for implementation, tests, CI configuration, documentation updates, and local validation, but not for long-term operational support.
Existing project conventions, dependency management, REST models, StreamController abstractions, ModuleLauncher code, and XD-to-s-c-s migration patterns can be reused.
The Redis counter is a single existing XD counter behavior that needs adaptation, not a redesign of the Redis data model or dashboard protocol.

REST stream commands include the core lifecycle and command operations already represented by StreamController; authentication, authorization, rate limiting, and production API versioning are out of scope.
External dependency handling is limited to resolving, packaging, and loading module-dependent JARs; dynamic hot replacement and arbitrary runtime plugin isolation are out of scope.

The PHD/HDFS investigation includes source inspection, dependency analysis, a small proof of concept or compatibility test, and a documented recommendation, but not complete HDFS module productionization.
CI uses standard hosted runners and does not require provisioning private build infrastructure, custom Docker registries, or deployment environments.
Estimates include normal code review preparation, test updates, and concise developer documentation, but exclude waiting time for external reviews or unavailable third-party systems.
No major undocumented security, performance, backward-compatibility, or migration requirement is discovered during implementation.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the relevant repositories, build files, existing controllers, launcher behavior, XD modules, Redis integrations, dependency-loading code, and current CI patterns; establish implementation boundaries and an execution plan.

Create curl or equivalent shell invocations for StreamController operations, configure representative request payloads, and add repeatable smoke validation for successful and common failure responses.
Port the XD Redis counter behavior into the spring-cloud-stream-modules conventions, implement configuration and message handling, add Redis interaction tests, and document module usage.
Add repository CI workflows for checkout, Java setup, dependency caching, compilation, tests, packaging, and pull-request or commit execution; validate the workflow on representative changes.

activities.activity_name: Module dependency resolution and Boot loader integration
activities.activity_description: Design and implement resolution of module-dependent JARs, integrate the resolved artifacts into the Spring Boot loader or executable classpath, handle representative database-driver dependencies, and add failure-path and integration tests.

Convert ModuleLauncher to a Spring Boot-based executable application, preserve existing launch behavior, externalize properties and settings, expose configuration needed by future classpath augmentation, and add launcher tests.

activities.activity_name: PHD and HDFS dependency approach investigation
activities.activity_description: Analyze PHD provider and HDFS dependency requirements, compare classpath and provider-loading approaches, build a focused compatibility proof of concept, and record the recommended implementation and risks.

Implement REST endpoints and request/response handling for stream lifecycle and command operations backed by StreamController, including validation, error mapping, controller tests, and integration coverage.
Add CI workflows for the modules repository covering the required Java and build matrix, tests, packaging, dependency caching, and commit or pull-request execution.
Run end-to-end checks across launcher, dependency loading, REST commands, and the adapted counter; update usage documentation, configuration examples, and troubleshooting notes.
Perform clean builds, regression testing, static checks, CI workflow validation, test-result review, defect correction for discovered issues, and prepare the final change set.
